Question
========
Consider the following XML document:

```
<location>
  <bike number="190301" state="ok"><battery_pack/></bike>
  <bike number="190302" state="ok"><battery_pack/></bike>
  <bike number="190303" state="error"><battery_pack/></bike>
</location>
```

What does the XPath expression `//bike[@state="error"]` select here?

Answerlist
----------
* Only the very first `bike` element in the document, no matter what its state is.
* All `bike` elements anywhere in the document whose `state` attribute equals `"error"` - in this case, the bike with number `"190303"`.
* Every element in the document that contains the word "error" somewhere in its text.
* Nothing, since XPath expressions cannot filter elements by their attribute values.


Solution
========
The `//` at the start means "search anywhere in the document", `bike` selects elements with that name, and `[@state="error"]` keeps only those where the `state` attribute has the value `"error"`. Applied to the document above, this matches exactly one element: the third `bike`, with `number="190303"`.

Answerlist
----------
* False
* True
* False
* False
